title: Edmund and the Crown
premise: Yara Sterling, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent years smuggling contraband through the Thornfell mountains while the old gods sleep and her magic fades. When prayers begin to be answered again, Yara discovers the god answering them is a devouring entity that has bound itself to King Edmund's crown — and it is eating the king alive from the inside. Hunted by the crown's zealots and shadowed by a found family of outcasts she never meant to love, Yara must choose between the oath that keeps her power alive and the people who keep her heart beating. In the end she breaks her own oath to sever the crown's binding, saving Edmund but losing her swordspeech forever — and discovering that what remains of her is enough.
about_author: Hazel Amberdale is the pen name of a former cartographer who once mapped mountain passes for a living and now maps imaginary ones instead. They write fantasy about stubborn people, old debts, and the geography of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Salt Road at Dusk
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She guides a smuggled cargo of prayer-tokens through the Thornfell passes, trading wry banter with her crew: gruff cook Bramble, runaway scribe Fen, and ex-soldier Osk. The emotional beat is weary competence masking loneliness — Yara insists she works alone even as she orchestrates everyone's survival.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Testing a stolen prayer-token on a lark, Fen whispers a wish for safe passage — and the mountain itself shifts to grant it. Terror ripples through the crew; the gods have been silent for a century. Yara privately recognizes the answering presence as something hungry, not holy.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A royal convoy forces Yara to guide them over the pass; inside it rides King Edmund, gaunt and flickering between lucidity and something else speaking through his mouth. He begs Yara, in a moment of clarity, to kill him before the coronation renewal rites. She refuses — and can't stop thinking about it.

chapters.title: Oath-Bound
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with flashback. We learn how swordspeakers swore their oaths to the old gods for power, and how Yara alone survived the purging of her order. Her fading magic stirs when near Edmund — proof the crown-thing feeds on oaths. Emotional beat: dread that her survival was never accident.

chapters.title: The Zealot's Ledger
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. Crown inquisitor Serah Vane arrives in the lowland town hunting 'god-touched' smugglers, carrying a ledger of names — including every member of Yara's crew. Osk, once Vane's comrade, must decide whether to warn the family he claims is temporary.

chapters.title: Bargains in the Dark
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Edmund escapes his handlers and finds Yara's camp, offering her anything for death. Instead she proposes a third path: unbind him from the crown using the lost rites of her order. He laughs — the first honest sound he's made in months — and agrees. Fragile alliance formed.

chapters.title: The Library That Walks
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. The crew seeks the Rites of Unbinding in the Wandering Scriptorium, a monastery that migrates through the mountains. Fen bargains with its blind archivist, paying memories as toll. Beat: found family deepens as each member offers a memory to cover Fen's shortfall.

chapters.title: Rites Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The rite requires an oath-breaker's blood and a willing vessel — and warns that unbinding will strip the swordspeaker of all power. Yara hides this from the crew. Edmund, reading her face, understands anyway and says nothing. Quiet devastation.

chapters.title: Serah Vane Closes In
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane captures Bramble and offers him clemency for Yara's location. Bramble gives nothing, but Vane deduces the route regardless. Interleaved: Bramble in chains reciting recipes to stay calm — the chapter's tender, stubborn heart.

chapters.title: Ambush at Hollow Bridge
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. Vane's soldiers ambush the party at the bridge; Osk reveals himself as a former royal blade to buy time, and takes wounds meant for Fen. Yara's dormant power flares violently when Edmund bleeds nearby — confirming the crown-thing wants her as much as him.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV (first time). Through the crown's eyes we see the entity's true nature: a starving god imprisoned beneath Thornfell long ago, using the monarchy as its anchor chain. It offers Edmund visions of a healed kingdom if he stops resisting. He nearly says yes.

chapters.title: Confessions by Firelight
chapters.summary: Yara and Edmund, two-hander scene. He confesses he invited the god in, desperate after plague took his heirs; she confesses the rite will cost her everything. Neither asks the other to stop. The emotional beat is two people falling in love precisely because they refuse to lie.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Salt Cells
chapters.summary: Full crew POV rotation. The team raids Vane's holding cells to free Bramble; Fen's stolen scriptorium knowledge unlocks the doors, Osk duels his past, and Yara walks out untouched because Vane hesitates — recognizing something of herself in Yara's devotion.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Recovered Bramble confronts Yara about her hidden sacrifice, having pieced it together from the rite's text. The crew demands she let someone else pay it. There is no one else. Beat: anger as a language of love; Yara holds firm.

chapters.title: Coronation Eve
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. The renewal rite approaches; the crown-thing's influence floods the capital, citizens praying themselves into ecstatic servitude. Vane, offered ascension as the god's new high priestess, feels her certainty crack when she sees children among the kneeling.

chapters.title: Infiltrating the Golden Hall
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Using smugglers' routes — the book's opening roads turned against the palace — the crew infiltrates the capital. Each member plays their role one last time. Rising tension: the plan requires Edmund to willingly sit the throne during the unbinding, exposed to the god.

chapters.title: The Renewal Rite
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Crowned before the assembled court, Edmund fights the entity from within while Yara begins the unbinding below the dais. Vane must choose: complete the ritual or cut Yara down. She lowers her blade — and is struck down by the god's faithful instead.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax, Yara's POV. The rite tears open; the god offers Yara her order restored, her power made whole, if she binds herself in Edmund's place. Speaking her oath-breaking aloud — 'I am done surviving alone' — she severs the binding. Her swordspeech dies screaming out of her.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Miracle
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Edmund lives, mortal and ordinary; the court reels; Vane clings to life and to doubt. The crew tends Yara, who cannot feel the old gods anymore and doesn't yet know who she is without them. Grief and relief braided together.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Without Chains
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund publicly renounces divine right, breaking the crown's enchantment in law as well as spirit. He offers Yara a place at his side — as equal, not champion. She asks for time. He gives it, which is exactly why she might say yes.

chapters.title: The Road Back Through Thornfell
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The crew travels home through the same pass where the story began. Bramble cooks, Fen writes, Osk limps contentedly, and Yara's hands are just hands now. When a traveler prays at a wayside shrine, something small and kind answers. The gods remain — changed, like her.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Crown
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating close-third between Yara and Edmund. Spring in the capital: Edmund without his crown visits the mountains under a plain name, and Yara meets him at the salt road's edge not as a subject or a sword, but as a choice freely renewed. Closing beat: love chosen daily, duty transformed into devotion.
